title: Toddler Science
subject: Science
philosophy: Science for toddlers is wonder, noticing and handling real things. Children learn about their bodies, the world around them and how things behave by looking, listening, touching, smelling, pouring, pushing and asking "what is it?" ELA’s Toddler Science keeps every experience hands-on, safe and short, and builds the words children need to talk about what they discover.
rationale: Early science is the foundation for later enquiry. Toddlers who handle water, sand, soil, plants and animals, and who hear the right words while they explore, build the vocabulary and curiosity that later science lessons depend on. This programme uses the familiar Nigerian environment (the market, the compound, the school garden, the rain and the harmattan) so that learning is rooted in what children already see and know.
aims: To encourage curiosity by letting children explore real objects, materials and living things.
To teach the names of body parts and the five senses through safe, playful activities.
To introduce simple ideas about materials, movement, living things and weather through play.
To build early science vocabulary such as soft, hard, wet, dry, push, pull, float and grow.
To teach caring habits: caring for living things, keeping clean and looking after the environment.
learningOutcomes: Names and points to main parts of the body and says what they are used for.
Uses the senses to explore and describes things with simple words such as soft, hard, hot and cold.
Explores water, sand and soil and notices that some things float and some sink.
Names familiar animals and plants and says where they live and what they need.
Describes the weather today with a word or gesture.
Pushes and pulls objects and notices that some things roll and slide.
Sorts everyday objects by simple properties such as colour, size or texture with support.
Shows care for living things and for the environment, for example by watering plants and putting litter in a bin.
Follows simple hygiene routines such as washing hands.
developmentalExpectations: Toddlers learn through their senses and through movement, so every lesson starts with real objects.
Attention is short; each activity is brief and repeated across the week.
Language grows with experience; adults name what children touch and see.
Toddlers do not yet explain why things happen; they notice, handle and describe.
Safety is essential: nothing small enough to swallow, no sharp or hot items, and adult supervision at all times.
keyCompetencies: Naming and describing objects and materials.
Caring for living things and the environment.

priorKnowledge: None assumed. Children bring many experiences of the home and the outdoors. Observe during the first two weeks how each child explores objects and records it as the baseline.
yearProgression: Term 1 focuses on me and my world: the body, the senses, water, sand and soil, and weather.
Term 2 focuses on living things: animals, their homes and babies, insects, plants, seeds, food and caring for living things.
Term 3 focuses on how things work: push and pull, rolling and sliding, light and shadow, wet and dry, natural and made things, colours in nature, health and caring for the environment.
assessmentPrinciples: Assessment is by watching, listening and recording what children say and do during play. There are no written tests.
Levels Emerging, Developing, Secure and Exceeding follow the lesson success criteria (see ASSESSMENT_FRAMEWORK.md).
Note the words children use to describe what they find, as evidence of learning.
Share with parents in plain language, always with a strength, a next step and a home idea.
inclusion: Every lesson has a support and an extension version.
Offer several ways to explore the same thing: look, touch, listen and move.
For children who dislike messy materials, offer a tool such as a spoon or a glove and never force.
Accept home-language words and repeat them in English in a natural way.
crossCurricular: Literacy: stories, rhymes and songs about animals, weather and plants.
Numeracy: sorting, counting objects and comparing size, weight and capacity.
Social Habits: hygiene, sharing equipment and caring for living things.
EYFS mapping: Understanding the World and Physical Development, with Communication and Language (see STANDARDS_ALIGNMENT.md).
parentConnection: Every lesson ends with a short home idea that uses safe household objects and the outdoors.
Parents are invited to share local plants, animals, foods and weather words from their home language.
Families are invited to help with the school garden and the nature table.

objectives: Children will point to and name main parts of the body.
Children will show what different body parts can do.
expectedOutcomes: Points to at least six body parts when named.
Says what a body part can do with support.

objectives: Children will use their eyes to find, match and name objects.
Children will use their ears to find and name sounds.
expectedOutcomes: Finds a hidden object by looking.
Names a sound heard in the room.

objectives: Children will touch and describe soft and hard objects.
Children will describe rough and smooth with support.
expectedOutcomes: Says soft or hard for a familiar object.
Sorts objects into soft and hard with support.

objectives: Children will smell safe items and say if they like the smell.
Children will taste safe foods and describe them with a word.
expectedOutcomes: Names a smell with support.
Says one word for how a food tastes.

objectives: Children will use different senses at stations to explore objects.
Children will link a sense to a body part.
expectedOutcomes: Names at least three senses with support.
Points to the body part for each sense.

objectives: Children will pour, splash and play with water safely.
Children will say whether things are wet or dry.
expectedOutcomes: Pours water from one container to another.
Says wet or dry for objects.

objectives: Children will put objects in water and see which float or sink.
Children will say float or sink with support.
expectedOutcomes: Says float or sink after seeing an object in water.
Puts a floating object on the water.

objectives: Children will play with sand and soil using hands and tools.
Children will notice that wet sand and dry sand feel different.
expectedOutcomes: Digs or scoops sand or soil with a tool.
Says wet or dry for sand.

objectives: Children will notice and name the weather each day.
Children will choose clothes for different weather with support.
expectedOutcomes: Names the weather today with a word or gesture.
Chooses suitable clothes for rain or sun with support.

objectives: Children will show Term 1 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 1 record.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with confidence at play stations.
Each child has an observation record for Term 1.

objectives: Children will name familiar animals and say where they see them.
Children will move like different animals.
expectedOutcomes: Names at least six animals.
Moves like an animal on request.

objectives: Children will match animals to their homes.
Children will say simple words for animal homes.
expectedOutcomes: Matches at least three animals to their homes.
Names one animal home.

objectives: Children will match animal babies to their mothers.
Children will say that mothers care for their babies.
expectedOutcomes: Matches at least three animal babies to their mothers.
Says "baby" and the animal name.

objectives: Children will look closely at small creatures with a magnifying glass.
Children will say that small creatures are looked at and not hurt.

objectives: Children will name trees, flowers and leaves and say that plants are alive.
Children will explore the school garden with their senses.
expectedOutcomes: Names a tree, a flower and a leaf.
Says that plants grow.

objectives: Children will plant a seed and water it.
Children will notice and talk about changes as the seed grows.
expectedOutcomes: Plants a seed with support.
Says "grow" or points to change.

objectives: Children will sort leaves by size and shape with support.
Children will name fruits and say they come from plants.

Names two fruits that grow on trees.

objectives: Children will say which foods come from plants and which from animals.

expectedOutcomes: Names two plant foods and two animal foods.

objectives: Children will water plants and say that plants need water.
Children will show kind and gentle handling of animals.
expectedOutcomes: Waters a plant with support.
Handles a toy animal gently.

objectives: Children will show Term 2 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 2 record.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with growing independence.

objectives: Children will push and pull toys and say push or pull.

expectedOutcomes: Pushes and pulls a toy on request.
Says push or pull with support.

objectives: Children will test objects to see which roll and which slide.

objectives: Children will notice that light comes from the sun and a torch.
Children will make and watch shadows.
